symptom: Live tree (doc_id=49d1bae2-af4d-4866-9399-f2a08e491440, verdict PASS) has 257 nodes / 9,436,085 chars (~31k chars/page over 292 pages, ~10x expected density) and only 1 of 20 <!-- image --> markers enriched with OCR chart text.
root_cause: Two independent, unrelated defects, neither in pageindex's chunk-concatenation or fallback code. (1) Char inflation: verified 80% of the 9.4M chars document-wide is whitespace (non-whitespace content is only ~1.89M chars, ~6.5k chars/page -- much closer to expected). Root cause is Docling's own document.export_to_markdown() table renderer: for irregular/dense per-country statistical table rows that don't cleanly parse into TableFormer's recognized column grid, it (a) assigns the SAME row text to every detected column (verified directly in the 'Finland' node: e.g. 'Fertility rate, total (live births per woman) 1.9 1.6 1.4 a,c' is repeated byte-identically 5-8x across pipe-delimited columns in one row) and (b) pads every cell in a table to the widest cell's width for GFM alignment (median whitespace run ~1031 chars/cell in Finland's table, 392 such runs). _pdf_to_markdown_docling_chunked (converters.py:2289-2375) simply concatenates two 146-page chunk markdowns unchanged -- no duplication introduced there -- and _document_level_text_fallback (converters.py:1640-1703) never fires for this doc (its 100-char / 50-chars-per-heading thresholds are far below this doc's dense per-chunk content). (2) The 19/20 unenriched markers are NOT a splice_picture_text_for_tree guard rejection (converters.py:1994-2031): that guard is all-or-nothing (returns md completely unchanged when marker_count != len(pics)), so if it had fired the result would be 0/20 enriched, not 1/20. Observing exactly 1 successful splice proves marker_count==len(pics)==20 held, i.e. the guard did NOT fire and the chunked-concatenation marker/pic-count invariant was NOT broken for this doc. The actual cause is that _recover_picture_text (invoked via _recover_picture_results, converters.py:2107-2158) returned empty OCR text for 19 of the 20 Docling-detected picture regions -- consistent with those regions being non-text decorative graphics (cover art/UN emblem/icons) rather than chart images with embedded text; only the first region (a cover-page paragraph rendered as an image) yielded real OCR text ('Department of Economic and Social Affairs...'). No evidence of a timed-out chunk falling back to PyPDF2 text extraction was found (that would produce a genuine marker/pic mismatch and skip splicing entirely, i.e. 0/20, not 1/20); with MAX_DOCLING_PAGES=150 this doc only produces 2 chunks and all 20 image markers cluster at the document start, consistent with a single non-timed-out chunk producing them all.
suggested_fix: 1) Add a post-export table-repair pass after export_to_markdown() calls (converters.py:2460,2525,2822) that detects degenerate rows where all column cells in a pipe-table row are byte-identical and collapses them to a single cell, and re-emits tables with minimal (single-space) column padding instead of relying on Docling's GFM-aligned padding -- this alone should recover most of the ~10x char inflation cheaply since it's purely a rendering-format issue, not lost/wrong data. 2) Instrument _recover_picture_results/_recover_picture_text to log a skip_reason histogram (e.g. counts of 'ocr_empty' vs 'guard_skip') so future audits can distinguish 'guard rejected the whole splice' from 'OCR legitimately found no text in a decorative region' without manual node inspection. 3) No fix required for the 19 unenriched markers themselves unless a crop-by-crop review shows they are genuinely text-bearing charts being missed by Tesseract -- current evidence points to them being non-text decorative graphics, which is correct (not a bug) behavior.
